Excellent remake of the 2002 classic. There has been significant content added, and the game is more fun than ever. I only play multiplayer, and I must warn other Mac players that queue times take a few minutes. There is no crossplay, so other means of playing the Windows version may become necessary for multi-player in the long-term.

citations.review_text: Never even got to play it. The broken update from almost two months ago left it unable to start. How hard is it to retract a broken update? AOE IV has the same problem.

I know this game is great, I played it all the time when I was kid. But I had to give this one a thumbs down for advertising in the description that it work on OS when in fact it doesn't. It crashes at the startup every time. Even when I've changed the setting to bypass it and start directly in the game it still crashes. Tried integrity check still didn't work. I have a Macbook pro M5. It says on the description M1 and over so there shouldn't be any issues. I'm really disappointed and I was looking forward to the nostalgic gameplay. If they ever fix this issue, I'll definitely buy it again in a heartbeat and change my review...

I work retail and hate the gut-renching feeling of receiving a bad review, and I rarely do this sort of thing... I dropped $12 bucks and I can't even play this game. It doesn't start, I have spent hours scouring the internet, reddits, forums etc. etc. to no avail.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the online multiplayer as highly competitive, noting that players must learn specific strategies or reach high villager build benchmarks quickly to win.

citations.review_text:
I played this game since 1999 and it's one of my favourites of all time, that was until this Definitive Edition was released.
There's such an overcrowding of new civs post Conquerors Edition that IMO don't even need to be inside the game, it's just being added for the sake of DLC and 'new content'.
The HD edition thrived and boomed, the standalone private servers before that were very active and lead to this game being made in the first place. I cant recommend this one for any long term fan of the series, the game has been min-maxed to hell and back, if you do not learn certain strats you become victim to one in the first 8 minutes of ANY ELO game, whether its being rushed by Cav or Castle Age rushed.

Any online game forces you to place a certain way or have the worst time possible, the game is now far too complicated for this AND the 100 civs currently in game, the average player cant and wont learn them all. 
HD edition is calling me back, it's cheaper, smaller on memory and the community of players don't grief you if you don't follow pro strats. 
This game is a bloated mess, but I can respect what the devs attempt to do to milk as much cash from this cow as possible.

Love the game but, the online mode has become part of the MOST ELITE so its IMPOSSIBLE to win unless you magically get 30 villagers in 10 minutes. I CANNOT win any. So i'm just leaving my salty review. 15 years of AoE and this literally was my triggering point. Rated system is clunky and I get paired with people with chinese/japan symbols for a name.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the remaster includes updated graphics, re-recorded audio scores, and quality-of-life interface improvements like automatic farm reseeding.

citations.review_text: If you've played Age of Empires 2 when it first came out, this remaster has earned it's definitive edition title. If you haven't, there is a reason why fans still play this game decades after it was released. The remastered visuals and audio are excellent, the gameplay is as solid as ever, and the online play is still active as of this posting and are till receiving updates and bug fixes as well.

AoE 2 DE epitomizes the pinnacle of real-time strategy remastering. It exquisitely revitalizes the cherished 1999 classic whilst preserving its intrinsic tactical enchantment. The breathtaking 4K visuals, meticulously re-recorded orchestral score, and indispensable enhancements in user experience, such as the automatic reseeding of farms, render the gameplay remarkably seamless in contemporary context. Featuring an astonishing array of historical civilizations, expansive single-player narratives, and a flourishing competitive multiplayer environment, the strategic profundity is unparalleled. Whether one is a wistful veteran or an inquisitive neophyte, this rendition unequivocally solidifies the game’s enduring legacy as an unequivocal masterpiece of magnificent medieval warfare simulation.
This is a welcome update to the graphics of the classic AOE 2, with the added bonus of new civilisations and maps.  Fantastic!

Its starting to look like a Paradox game. 2 $20 DLCs a year that only partially function to keep milking the IP. I cannot recommend a game which costs more than three times the advertised price to get the full game.

That said, It runs marvelously smooth. A lot of clunky mechanics have been fixed, and mod support is very good. As a remake of Age of Kings it is very well done.

**Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition** is one of the best real-time strategy games ever made. Even after so many years, it remains incredibly fun thanks to its excellent gameplay, constant updates, and active community. Whether you're playing against AI, friends, or online opponents, every match feels different and rewarding.

What I enjoy the most is the strategic depth. Every civilization has its own unique strengths, technologies, and units, which means there are countless ways to approach a match. Resource management, base building, military production, and timing your attacks all require careful planning. Winning through a well-executed strategy is extremely satisfying.

The Definitive Edition also brings major improvements over the original game. The graphics are much sharper, the animations are smoother, and the soundtrack has been beautifully remastered. In addition, the developers continue to release balance updates, new civilizations, and expansions, keeping the game fresh for both new and veteran players.

Another great feature is the amount of content available. There are dozens of civilizations, hundreds of historical campaigns, custom scenarios, ranked multiplayer, and an active modding community. Even after hundreds of hours, there's still something new to learn or experience.

If I had to mention a downside, it would be the learning curve. Multiplayer can be difficult for beginners because experienced players know optimized build orders and strategies. It takes time and practice to become competitive, but the process of improving is also one of the game's greatest strengths.

Overall, Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition is a masterpiece of the RTS genre. It combines strategy, history, and replayability better than almost any other game. If you enjoy strategy games, this is an essential title that I highly recommend.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players point out matchmaking penalties, recent launch instability, and strict Mac platform barriers.

claims.claim: Ranked matchmaking restricts the Mac version to Mac-only multiplayer, cutting players off from the broader community.

citations.review_text: The mac version has some bug that kicks me out from a queue and then says "This account recently disconnected from a matchmaking game early" and the waiting time to join the queue again is around an hour.

So Feral brought Age of Empire II back to mac.
It works, for solo play.

However, they decided to restrict multiplayer to mac only, so the whole mac version is cut off from the multiplayer community which is the reason this 20+ year old game is still relevant today.

My friends don't have macs, I'd like to play with them.

Age of Empires II runs under Asahi Linux, and supports multiplayer with others quite reliably.

Until Feral publishes a good explanation of why cross-platform multiplayer is technically impossible, (or a roadmap on enabling it) you should probably refrain from buy this to play on a mac, just buy the steam version from a PC / Linux+Steam+Proton and play through Asahi Linux if you have a mac.

(It used to be that running on VMWare Fusion would cause multiplayer game to desync, but I haven't tried again recently, nor have I tried Parallel).
